ui_bugs.issue: React hydration warning: '<a> cannot be a descendant of <a>' / '<a> cannot contain a nested <a>'. The card's outer element is a <Link> (renders <a>) wrapping the whole card, and the seller-company <Link> (also renders <a>, with data-testid=activity-card-seller-link-*) is nested inside it. This produces invalid nested-anchor HTML. Functionally the stopPropagation() on the inner link click still prevents double-navigation (verified working), but this is invalid HTML and triggers a React hydration mismatch warning in the console on every category/company list page load. Recommend restructuring so the outer card container is a <div onClick=navigate> (or similar) instead of a <Link>, keeping only leaf-level Links/buttons as actual anchors.

rca_of_the_issue: Nested-anchor warning RCA: ActivityListPage.jsx wraps the entire excursion card in <Link to='/activities/view/:alias'> (renders <a>), and inside the card body it renders another <Link to='/activities/company/:slug'> (also renders <a>) for the seller name, with onClick={(e)=>e.stopPropagation()} to stop the click from bubbling to the outer Link. This correctly prevents double-navigation in practice (verified: clicking the seller link navigates only to the company page), but HTML5 forbids nested <a> elements, so React logs a hydration mismatch warning on every render of this page. Mitigation: replace the outer <Link> wrapper with a <div> that has an onClick handler calling navigate(), or use React Router's useNavigate() on a non-anchor wrapper, keeping the inner seller <Link> as the only real anchor in that region.
